section_summary: This concluding section contains a January 1946 U.S. Embassy despatch forwarding photostatic copies from the archives of the former Japanese Legation in Panama. Its surviving enclosure is a Japanese Foreign Ministry statistical booklet, dated April 1, 1941, tabulating Japanese and third-country nationals in China by region, locality, and consular district; it also includes an errata table and U.S. custodial markings dated September 21, 1945. The despatch states that the larger copied set also covered a code book and card indexes requested by the Chinese Legation in Panama.

people.name: V. Lansing Collins, Jr.
people.role: Second Secretary of the U.S. Embassy in Panama; signed the despatch for the Ambassador

subfiles.title: Transmitting Set of Photostatic Copies of Certain Portions of the Former Japanese Legation in Panama
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy in Panama, V. Lansing Collins, Jr., Second Secretary
subfiles.about: Forwards photostatic copies of selected records from the archives of the former Japanese Legation in Panama.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy refers to its earlier despatch No. 2857 of October 1, 1945, which inventoried the remains of the Japanese archives in Panama. It forwards copies made at the request of the Chinese Legation, including population statistics, a code book, 43 orange cards, and 266 white cross-index cards. The despatch is numbered 690 and classified secret.

subfiles.title: 中華民國在留本邦人及第三國人人口概計表 (Approximate Population Table of Japanese and Third-Country Nationals Resident in the Republic of China)
subfiles.from: Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, East Asia Bureau, Third Division
subfiles.about: Presents population statistics for Japanese and third-country nationals residing in China, organized by region, locality, and consular jurisdiction.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure opens with a Japanese title page dated April 1, 1941, followed by a contents page and an errata table referring to figures as of January 1, 1941. The remaining pages consist largely of densely printed demographic tables comparing categories of residents and arranging counts by consular district and locality, including Xiamen and Xiaozhan. Several sheets bear custodial markings identifying them as material from the Japanese Legation in Panama dated September 21, 1945; pages 624 and 629 yield no OCR text but form part of the enclosure.
